ukmt-grey-2021-20.title: Build the smallest number
ukmt-grey-2021-20.body:
Four digits give at most $4\times9=36<41$, so $N$ has at least 5 digits. To make $N$ as small as possible, use exactly 5 digits and make the first digit as small as possible, so the other four digits are all 9 (sum 36). The first digit is then $41-36=5$, so $N=59\,999$.

$N+2021=59\,999+2021=62\,020$, and its digit sum is $6+2+0+2+0=10$.

**Answer: (A) 10**

ukmt-grey-2021-20.title: Use a shortcut
ukmt-grey-2021-20.body:
Once $N=59\,999=60\,000-1$ is found, $N+2021=60\,000+2020=62\,020$ without any carrying, and the digit sum is $6+2+2=10$.

**Answer: (A) 10**

ukmt-grey-2021-22.title: Equate the travelling times
ukmt-grey-2021-22.body:
Let the distance be $x$ km. When they meet, Geraint has cycled $x-105$ km, taking $\frac{x-105}{30}$ hours. Lewis has driven to Beetown and $105$ km back, so $x+105$ km, taking $\frac{x+105}{70}$ hours of driving plus 1 hour of stopping. They travelled for the same total time:

$$\frac{x-105}{30}=\frac{x+105}{70}+1.$$

Multiplying by 210: $7(x-105)=3(x+105)+210$, so $4x=1260$ and $x=315$.

**Answer: (A) 315 km**

ukmt-grey-2021-22.title: Check the answer
ukmt-grey-2021-22.body:
For $x=315$: Geraint has cycled $210$ km, which takes $210\div30=7$ hours. Lewis has driven $315+105=420$ km, which takes $420\div70=6$ hours, plus 1 hour stopped, so also 7 hours. The equation above is linear, so this is the only solution.

**Answer: (A) 315 km**
